question.worked_solution:
In the equation, $c$ is being divided by $7.$ To isolate $c$, we can perform the opposite operation, which is *multiplying* by $7.$ So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $7.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{c}{7} & =-15 \\ 7\cdot \frac{c}{7} & =7\cdot (-15) \\ \frac{7c}{7} & =-105\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $7$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{7c}{7} & =-105 \\ \frac{\cancel{7}c}{\cancel{7}} & =-105 \\ c & =-105\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
